resources.string: Soft mode
A pause and a gentle nudge when you open something distracting. Nothing is forced.
Sealed mode
Your normal home screen stays. Distracting apps disappear from it and go quiet.
Off: Sealed disappears from the mode picker. Block still stops apps opening, it just leaves them sitting on your home screen.
Kiosk mode
Pinehold becomes the whole phone for a set stretch of time. The strongest setting there is.
Kiosk is the only mode that closes Safe Mode and the launcher. Without it there is a way back out.
Let me end a session early
Shows an \"End this session\" button while a session is running.
Off: there is no early exit. The session runs to the end of its timer, and in Kiosk the only way out before then is a factory reset, which wipes the phone.
Freeze my rules while a session runs
Once a session starts, rules, app policies and these switches stop being editable until it ends. Stops the 11pm version of you from quietly unblocking something.

Off: you can change any rule mid-session, including ending a Kiosk early. Some people want that and it is a fair choice — it just means the lock is only as strong as you are at the moment you want to break it.
Actually stop blocked apps
A blocked app does not open at all. Turn this off and you get a pause screen you can walk through instead.
Off: blocked apps still open. You get a reminder first, and then you decide. That is Soft mode\'s behaviour, applied to whatever mode you are in.
App blocking
Stop chosen apps from opening while a session is running.
With this off, every app on the phone opens normally. That is your call.
Web blocking
Hold the browser to your allowlist and keep the open internet out of Chrome.
With this off, any site loads in any browser. That is your call.
Custom rules
Your own if-this-then-that rules: a target, a condition, an outcome.
Always-allowed apps
Essentials that stay open through everything: calls, maps, notes. Nothing overrides this list.
With this off, a session can cut off calls and maps too. Most people keep this on.
Breathing pause
A few slow seconds before a distracting app opens, with a way out. Often that is enough.
Off: apps you set to pause first open immediately, with no breath in between.
Take a break
Unlock a blocked app for a few minutes instead of abandoning the whole session.
Off: a blocked app stays blocked for the whole session, with no exceptions. Some people need exactly that. Others end the whole session instead of taking five minutes.
Daily limits
Give an app a daily budget of minutes or opens. When it runs out, it closes until tomorrow.
Off: daily budgets stop counting. Apps you limited open for as long as you like.
Daily open limits
Cap how many times an app can be opened in a day. Catches the reflex, not the minutes.
Earn mode
Finish real tasks to unlock leisure time. You set the rate, the reward and what counts as done.
Off: tasks stay a plain to-do list and finishing one earns nothing. The list still works, it just does not pay.
Content guard
Reads what is on screen and backs out of the surfaces you named, inside apps you still want.
Off: Pinehold stops reading the screen. An app you allowed is allowed entirely, including the parts of it you were trying to avoid.
Keyword guard
Your own words. If one shows up on screen, Pinehold steps back out of that screen.
WhatsApp guard
Keeps chats working while quietly closing Channels, Updates and Meta AI.
Telegram: only the chats you named
Keeps Telegram open for the people you actually talk to, and backs out of everything else. You list the chats that are allowed.
Off: every Telegram chat and channel opens normally.
Shorts blocker
Neutralises the YouTube Shorts shelf and player. The rest of YouTube still works.
Reels blocker
Closes Instagram, Facebook and Snapchat reel surfaces the moment they open.
Adult content filter
A maintained keyword and domain filter, on top of forced SafeSearch.
Schedules
Windows of the week where the phone goes quiet on its own.
Off: quiet windows stop firing. Every session becomes something you have to remember to start.
Bedtime
Dims the screen, switches to a dark quiet theme and locks social after your cut-off.
Off: nothing changes at night. The phone is as available at 2am as it is at 2pm.
Place rules
Block or allow apps depending on where you are. Social off at school, maps always on.
Network rules
Use the Wi-Fi you are on as a condition: home network, school network, mobile data.
Notification shield
Holds back alerts from blocked apps during a session. Always-allowed apps still get through.
Off: blocked apps can still buzz. The icon is out of reach but the pull is not.
Safe browser
A curated internet that opens instantly and has nowhere to fall into.
Text search
Google with the images, videos and thumbnails stripped out. Reading, not scrolling.
Video library
Your own folder, one new unlock every 24 hours. Yours to keep once opened.
Offer an alternative
When something is blocked, suggest a calm thing to do instead of a dead end.
Local analytics
Time by app and category, kept on this phone only. Nothing leaves the device.
Gentle streaks
Counts the days you showed up. A missed day pauses the count, it never shatters it.
Kind wording
Block screens speak plainly and without blame. Turn off for blunt, minimal wording.
Suspend blocked apps
Blocked apps become unopenable at the system level, not just intercepted.
With this off, blocked apps can still start for a moment before being caught.
Hide blocked apps
Blocked apps vanish from the launcher during a session. Out of sight, out of reach.
With this off, blocked apps stay on your home screen. They still will not open, but you see them every time you look.
Lock the notification shade
Holds back the notification shade during a kiosk session. Quick settings is already unavailable in any kiosk session — Android gives no way to keep it — so brightness lives in Always-allowed instead.
Leaving this off keeps the shade reachable, a common way back out mid-session.
Simplify the lock screen
Strips widgets and shortcuts off the lock screen while a kiosk session runs.
Block uninstalling Pinehold
Stops Pinehold itself being removed while a session is running.
With this off, a session can be ended by uninstalling the app.
Disable Safe Mode
Closes the Safe Mode reboot, which would otherwise start the phone with Pinehold inert.
Safe Mode is the classic way out. Leaving it open is a real escape route.
Modes
How strong the lock is allowed to get.
Blocking
What Pinehold is allowed to stop.
Content
Guards that read the screen, not just the app name.
Environment
Rules that follow time, place and network.
Replacements
The calm things Pinehold offers instead of the feed.
Insight
What Pinehold remembers and shows you about yourself.
Hardening
Escape routes you can choose to close.
Advanced
Places, Wi-Fi conditions, and custom if-this-then-that rules.
Experimental
Screen-reading guards for WhatsApp, Shorts, Reels, and Telegram. Off by default because app updates can change their layout.
Pinehold as home screen
During a kiosk session the home button lands here instead of the launcher.
With this off, the home button returns to your normal launcher mid-session.
%1$s is off
Let blockers work outside a session
Off: nothing blocks unless a session is running. On: Bedtime, schedules, limits, places, rules and guards also work on their own.
Works with no session only when \'Let blockers work outside a session\' is on
